items.t: Add-on symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea in infants over 3 months and children, together with oral rehydration.

src.q: Complementary symptomatic treatment of acute diarrhoea in infants (older than 3 months) and children together with oral rehydration (ORS).

items.t: Must be given with oral rehydration; it does not change usual rehydration regimens.

src.q: Hidrasec is administered via the oral route, together with oral rehydration (see section 4.4).
does not modify the usual rehydration regimens.

dosing.note: The clinic products (10 mg and 30 mg granules) are licensed for infants over 3 months and children only; see the paediatric section. Adult dosing not covered.

items.t: 1.5 mg/kg per dose three times daily at regular intervals. Under 9 kg: one 10 mg sachet three times daily; 9-13 kg: two 10 mg sachets three times daily.

src.q: 1.5 mg/kg per dose (corresponding to 1 to 2 sachets), three times daily at regular intervals.
In infant less than 9 kg : one 10 mg sachet 3 times daily. In infant from 9 kg to 13 kg : two 10 mg sachets 3 times daily.

items.t: 1.5 mg/kg per dose three times daily. 13-27 kg: one 30 mg sachet three times daily; over 27 kg: two 30 mg sachets three times daily.

src.q: 1.5 mg/kg per dose (corresponding to 1 to 2 sachets), three times daily at regular intervals.
In children from 13 kg to 27 kg : one 30 mg sachet 3 times daily. In children of more than 27 kg : two 30 mg sachets 3 times daily.

items.t: Continue until two normal stools; do not exceed 7 days.

src.q: Treatment should be continued until two normal stools are recorded. Treatment should not exceed 7 days.

items.t: Must not be given to infants under 3 months (no clinical trials).

src.q: The product must not be administered to infants less than 3 months old, as there are no clinical trials in this population.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to racecadotril or any excipient.

src.q: 4.3 Contraindications Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Contains sucrose: hereditary fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase deficiency should not take (listed in 4.3).

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome or saccharase- isomaltase deficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: Section 4.4 'must not' statements: infants under 3 months; children with renal or liver impairment of any degree; prolonged or uncontrolled vomiting; restarting after DRESS.

src.q: The product must not be administered to children with renal or liver impairment, whatever the degree of severity, due to a lack of information on these patient populations.
the product must not be administered in cases of prolonged or uncontrolled vomiting.

items.t: Bloody or purulent stools with fever (invasive bacteria or other severe disease) or antibiotic-associated diarrhoea: should not be given.

src.q: The presence of bloody or purulent stools and fever may indicate the presence of invasive bacteria as a reason for diarrhoea, or the presence of other severe disease.
Therefore, racecadotril should not be administered under these conditions.

items.t: Angioedema can occur at any time; airway involvement needs emergency treatment. Stop and supervise closely. Past angioedema not caused by racecadotril may raise the risk.

src.q: Where there is angioedema associated with upper airway obstruction, such as tongue, glottis and/or larynx, emergency therapy should be administered promptly.
Patients with a history of angioedema unrelated to racecadotril therapy may be at increased risk of angioedema.

items.t: Severe skin reactions including DRESS (can be fatal): stop immediately; never restart after DRESS.

src.q: If signs and symptoms suggestive of DRESS appear, racecadotril should be withdrawn immediately and an alternative treatment considered.
treatment with racecadotril must not be restarted in these patients at any time.

items.t: Severe or prolonged diarrhoea with marked vomiting or poor appetite: consider IV rehydration.

src.q: In the event of serious or prolonged diarrhoea with important vomiting or a lack of appetite, intravenous rehydration should be considered.

items.t: Diabetes: count the sucrose content if the daily dose provides more than 5 g sucrose. Chronic diarrhoea not sufficiently studied.

src.q: In patients with diabetes, it should be taken into account that each sachet contains 2.899 g of sucrose.
Chronic diarrhoea has not been sufficiently studied with this product.

items.t: Other medicines that cause bradykinin-mediated angioedema (ACE inhibitors; to a lesser extent angiotensin II antagonists, gliptins, mTOR inhibitors, sacubitril, alteplase, estramustine): combined use may raise angioedema risk and is not recommended.

src.q: The most frequently implicated drugs are ACE inhibitors, and to a lesser extent: angiotensin II antagonists
Concomitant use of racecadotril and other drugs known to cause bradykinin-mediated angioedema may increase the risk of angioedema and are not recommended

items.t: No clinically relevant inhibition or induction of major CYP enzymes in vitro.

src.q: do not inhibit the major CYP enzymes isoforms 3A4, 2D6, 2C9, 1A2 and 2C19 to an extent that would be clinically relevant.

items.t: Must not be given to children with renal impairment of any degree (no data). No eGFR or CrCl threshold given.

src.q: The product must not be administered to children with renal or liver impairment, whatever the degree of severity, due to a lack of information on these patient populations.

items.t: Must not be given to children with liver impairment of any degree (no data).

src.q: The product must not be administered to children with renal or liver impairment, whatever the degree of severity, due to a lack of information on these patient populations.

items.t: No adequate human data; should not be given to pregnant women.

src.q: However, since no specific clinical studies are available, Hidrasec should not be administered to pregnant women.

items.t: No data on excretion in milk: should not be given to breastfeeding women.

src.q: this medicinal product should not be administered to breastfeeding women.

items.t: Rat studies show no effect on fertility.

src.q: Fertility studies conducted with racecadotril on Rats demonstrate no impact on fertility.

items.t: No common adverse effects listed. Uncommon: tonsillitis, rash, erythema.

src.q: Uncommon: tonsillitis.
Uncommon: rash, erythema.

items.t: Angioedema (face, lips, tongue, larynx) and anaphylactic shock: emergency treatment if airway involved; stop racecadotril.

src.q: Racecadotril should be discontinued and the patient should be under close medical supervision
Unknown: anaphylactic shock.

items.t: Severe cutaneous reactions including DRESS (life-threatening or fatal): stop immediately and never restart.

src.q: Severe cutaneous adverse reactions (SCARs) including drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), which can be life-threatening or fatal, have been reported in association with racecadotril treatment.

items.t: Monitor closely for skin reactions; stop at signs of severe skin reaction or DRESS.

src.q: Patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.
When experiencing severe skin reactions, the treatment has to be stopped immediately.

items.t: Add the granules to food, or disperse in a glass of water or the feeding bottle; mix well and give immediately.

src.q: The granules can be added to food, dispersed in a glass of water or in the feeding-bottle, mixing well and followed by immediate administration.

items.t: Keep giving oral rehydration solution; racecadotril does not replace it.

src.q: Rehydration is highly important in the management of acute diarrhoea in infants.

items.t: Seek urgent help for swelling of the face, lips or tongue, or a severe rash.

src.q: Angioedema of the face, extremities, lips, mucous membranes may occur.
